questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a place that I had been before, so I knew I would love it. My friend had studied at the same university previously and she played a big part in making me consider South Korea.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Since I already had experience with the country it was quite easy to to figure things out. But I also have to add that Korea in general makes it easy to navigate the country and Seoul in general.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
They have many different apps that help foreigners and locals alike, and if that doesn't work the locals are always there to lend a helping hand.
When it comes to the school, they made it quite easy for exchange students to figure everything out by providing guides and tutorials through emails (like course sign up, payment etc.). Beforehand they also made sure to create a groupchat for all the exchange students so that students can ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: On goshipages you can find accommodation quite easily. You can filter by location and university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
When it comes to SKKU I know that many exchange students didn't like that there was a curfew. For students who want more freedom I would suggest to find accomodation off campus. 
Make sure to find housing early on before you arrive. I ended up living 3 different places, and the last place was the best. Goshiwons are very small, but it was the only place I could find on short notice, so if you want a good place then search early on.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: SKKU made it easy for us to register for courses, by providing guides on how to do it. Before registering, the website allows you to add your courses in a basket and then when its time for signing up you just have to click register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tutorials, guides, email assistance.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get all the courses I wanted in the first round, but one course ended up being cancelled and so I had to sign up for a new course in the 2nd round of sign ups. Even though many courses are full it is possible to contact the professor and ask if you can join, and most of the times they say yes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to sign up for course AS SOON AS IT OPENS. My friend made the mistake of waiting a few hours and almost all courses were full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The grading system in Korea is very different from the one in Denmark. Many factors count into your final grade such as midterm, participation, attendance, discussions, assignments etc. Though it was strange at first, it made it easier to pass courses since ones grade doesnt rely on only one factor.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level was easier but this might have been due to the amount of credit of the courses. I usually have two courses each semester but this time i had 5, which means the amount of credit for each course is significantly smaller.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed it a lot. Especially one course had a good balance of lectures mixed with student discussions where we could apply theory in praksis.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
*Convergence Media and Popular Culture 
*Understanding Computational Media 
*Political & Economic Development in Korea 
*Economics in Global Environments
*Popular Culture and Digital Media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Understanding computational media
Popular culture and digital media.
Both professors in these courses were amazing and it was clear to see how much they enjoyed teaching.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Communication. I bought an esim at the airport and it was much more expensive than any other place. Other people used Chingu mobile.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, clothes and smaller appliances (from daiso) can be found very cheap. At some places they are more expensive, but its usually around the same price. The reason why food expenses is the highest is because i ate out everyday and never cooked. Transportation is very cheap, since the price is the same no matter where and how far you go. If you need to find things for your house, go to daiso.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
SKKU offered many different clubs and most of them were also available to exchange students. The HI-club also hosts different events for exchange students so people can meet eachother. 
The university also has several festivals, such as movie night and koncerts where you can see famous singers like PSY (make sure to go).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the dance club Ggun and it was probably the best decision of my whole stay. I met so many different people and made a lot of friends and memories. And there is no need for dancing experience beforehand.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to nearby cities such as incheaon, nami island or even busan or jeju.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of small cultural differences but they were quite easy to adapt to. Like not talking/eating/drinking in the subway. They also have a lot of self-service at restaurants where you have to set your own table, bring side dishes and go up to the counter to pay when leaving.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make sure to take some major courses where there are Koreans! The korean friends I made were very welcoming and friendly but they might be a little shy in the beginning. Joining clubs also helps with meeting locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At times people might ignore you if you speak english to them since some locals are bit uncomfortable with speaking english.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Despite the previous statement, many people are very helpful even though there is a clear language barrier. Knowing a few korean words goes a long way.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join some clubs, become more extroverted if you can, and don't worry too much about grades - instead focus on enjoying your time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to walk up a hill everyday. Make sure to go to ESKARA and get some souvenirs. Try the robot coffee at the library.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all around the world and becoming friends with so many different people that I still wish to keep in contact with. I started out as an introvert but I knew that the best way to enjoy my stay would be to become more extroverted.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accommodation since I had to move three times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Download KakaoTalk, Kakaomap, Naver, and buy a transportation card as soon as possible.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
